authors: Han S, Zhang Y, Masunaga S, Zhou S, Naito W
title: Relating metal bioavailability to risk assessment for aquatic species: Daliao River watershed, China
water_body: Daliao River watershed (Daliao main channel incl. estuary sites D-3/D-4, Xi, Hun, Taizi rivers), 13 sites
location_in_paper: Table 1 (pH, DOC, Ca, temp per site); Table 2 (HC5, RCR = dissolved/HC5, DGT-labile/HC5 per site)
notes: Labile fraction derived per site as (DGT-labile/HC5)/RCR, because both ratios in Table 2 share the same site-specific HC5; dissolved = RCR x HC5 and C_DGT = (DGT-labile/HC5) x HC5. Ratios are printed to 2 decimals, so small cells (e.g. 0.03-0.07) carry up to ~15-30% rounding error. Cross-checks against text values agree for most sites (e.g. Ni D-3, Cu D-4, Zn D-3, dissolved Ni/Zn T-1), but T-1 is internally inconsistent: text gives DGT-labile Ni 0.28 and Cu 0.34 ug/L at T-1 whereas Table 2 implies ~0.50 and ~1.34 ug/L. DGT deployed in situ 24 h (2-4 units per site, Sep-Oct 2011), 0.45 um filtration. pH range only 7.47-8.64 (all circumneutral-alkaline). D-3 and D-4 are estuarine (Na 302-832 mg/L, Cl 308-427 mg/L) so ionic strength co-varies. Sources differ strongly between sites (industrial/municipal effluents), so dissolved and C_DGT slopes mainly reflect source strength; the fraction removes supply. OLS of log10(fraction) on pH, Pearson r. Sensitivity: excluding T-1 slope -0.235 (SE 0.140, n=12); excluding estuarine D-3/D-4 slope -0.143 (SE 0.119, n=11). Not significant in any version.

authors: Røyset O, Rosseland BO, Kristensen T, Kroglund F, Garmo ØA, Steinnes E
title: Diffusive gradients in thin films sampler predicts stress in brown trout (Salmo trutta L.) exposed to aluminum in acid fresh waters
water_body: River Tovdal inlet to Lake Tveitvatn, southern Norway (field test rig, 4 treatment lines x 3 tanks)
location_in_paper: Fig. 5 (DGT-Al and Ali vs pH) digitised; Table 1 (treatment means of pH, Ca, total Al, Alc, Alo, Ali)
notes: In-river field manipulation (Oct 2001): Ca(OH)2 additions raised pH (low Ca 5.4, high Ca 5.9), HCl/AlCl3 lowered pH to 4.8 and added Al (~+30 ug/L total Al), reference 5.2. 11 of 12 DGT deployments (4 lines x 0-7, 7-14, 0-14 d) resolved in Fig. 5 (one presumably hidden). Total Al (unfiltered, Table 1) was nearly constant across the reference/low Ca/high Ca lines (186-196 ug/L), so for those lines the C_DGT slope approximates a labile-fraction slope (DGT-Al/total Al ~0.15-0.33); AlCl3 spike confounds the two lowest-pH points. Excluding the two Al/H+ points (pH<5.0): slope -0.351 (SE 0.069, n=9). Authors: DGT also takes up 10-30% of organically complexed Al (Alo); above pH 5.5 Al(OH)3 precipitation controls Ali. Ca co-varies with pH (Ca(OH)2 addition), so the competing-cation effect is not separated. Pearson r.
